# Downloading a package by hand

This page is for administrators who want to see a package before an installer uses it, or who have to bring a
package to a server that cannot reach the package server. It shows how to download an `.ezpkg`, look inside it, check
it, and import it.

## Contents

1. [Find the address](#find-the-address)
2. [Download](#download)
3. [Look inside](#look-inside)
4. [Check it](#check-it)
5. [Find what it requires](#find-what-it-requires)
6. [Import it](#import-it)
7. [Related pages](#related-pages)

## Find the address

Every package's address is the `url` attribute of its entry in the release's `index.xml`. For 6.0.15 they all
follow one pattern:

```text
https://exponential.packages.exponential.earth/exponential/6.0/6.0.15/<name>.ezpkg
```

To list the names and types of a release:

```bash
curl -s https://exponential.packages.exponential.earth/exponential/6.0/6.0.15/index.xml \
  | grep -o '<package name="[^"]*"[^>]*type="[^"]*"' \
  | sed 's/<package name="\([^"]*\)".*type="\([^"]*\)"/\1 \2/'
```

Or open the release folder in a browser ([Browsing the package server](browsing-the-package-server-in-a-browser.md)).

## Download

Work in a folder of your own, for example `var/tmp/` of the installation, not in a shared temporary folder:

```bash
mkdir -p var/tmp/packages && cd var/tmp/packages
curl -fsSLO https://exponential.packages.exponential.earth/exponential/6.0/6.0.15/sevenx_multisite.ezpkg
```

| Option | Why |
|---|---|
| `-f` | fail on an HTTP error instead of saving the error page as the package |
| `-s`, `-S` | quiet, but still show errors |
| `-L` | follow a redirect (an `http://` address is redirected to `https://`) |
| `-O` | keep the file name of the URL |

`wget https://...` does the same. Behind a proxy, set it the way your tools expect (for curl `-x` or the
`https_proxy` variable).

## Look inside

An `.ezpkg` is a gzip compressed tar archive with the package folder's content at the top:

```bash
tar -tzf sevenx_multisite.ezpkg
```

```text
documents/
documents/LICENCE
files/
files/default/
files/default/image/
files/default/image/logo.png
files/default/thumbnail/
files/default/thumbnail/thumbnail.png
package.xml
settings/
settings/ini-admin.php
settings/sevenx-multi-site-installer.php
...
```

Read one file without unpacking:

```bash
tar -xzOf sevenx_multisite.ezpkg package.xml | less
```

Unpack into a folder of its own to read the rest:

```bash
mkdir sevenx_multisite && tar -xzf sevenx_multisite.ezpkg -C sevenx_multisite
```

What the files are: [The .ezpkg file](../basics/the-ezpkg-file.md) and
[package.xml reference](../basics/package-xml-reference.md).

## Check it

| Check | Command | Expect |
|---|---|---|
| It is gzip data | `file sevenx_multisite.ezpkg` | "gzip compressed data" |
| It is complete | `ls -l` and the `Content-Length` of `curl -sI <url>` | the same number of bytes |
| The archive is intact | `tar -tzf sevenx_multisite.ezpkg > /dev/null && echo ok` | `ok` |
| The definition is well formed | `tar -xzOf sevenx_multisite.ezpkg package.xml \| xmllint --noout -` | no output |
| No unsafe entries | `tar -tzvf sevenx_multisite.ezpkg \| grep -E '^[lhcbp]\|\.\./'` | no output (no links, devices, or `..` paths) |
| It is the file in Git | `sha256sum` of your file and of the same file in the server's repository | the same sum |

For the last check, the server's repository has every file with its history:

```bash
git clone --filter=blob:none https://github.com/se7enxweb/exponential.packages.exponential.earth.git
git -C exponential.packages.exponential.earth show HEAD:exponential/6.0/6.0.15/sevenx_multisite.ezpkg | sha256sum
```

The import applies its own checks as well: gzip signature, size and entry limits, only plain files and folders with
relative paths, a valid `package.xml` with a valid name. They are listed in the
[Packages guide, 6. Uploading a package](../../../guides/packages.md#6-uploading-a-package).

## Find what it requires

A site package rarely comes alone. Its `<requires>` names the other packages:

```bash
tar -xzOf sevenx_multisite.ezpkg package.xml | xmllint --xpath '//requires/require/@name' -
# or, to see min-version too:
tar -xzOf sevenx_multisite.ezpkg package.xml | grep -A2 '<require '
```

For `sevenx_multisite` that gives `sevenx_classes` and `sevenx_multisite_democontent`, each with
`min-version="5.1"`. Download those too, and their requirements in turn, before you take the packages to a server
without network access. See [Dependencies and the install order](../basics/dependencies-and-install-order.md).

## Import it

Importing puts the package into the local repository (`var/storage/packages/<vendor>/<name>/`) without changing the
site ([Import versus install](../basics/import-versus-install.md)). Three ways:

**On the command line**, from the installation root:

```bash
php ezpm.php import var/tmp/packages/sevenx_multisite.ezpkg
```

`ezpm.php import` takes the path of an `.ezpkg` in either package format and runs the same archive checks as the upload
page. It refuses a package whose name already exists in a repository ("Could not import package ..., it already
exists"). See [ezpm, the package manager on the command line](../../../features/6.0/ezpm-package-manager-cli.md).

**In the administration**: Setup > Packages, **Import new package**, choose the file, **Import package**
([Importing a package](../admin-gui/importing-a-package.md)).

**In the setup wizard**: on the **Site package** step, **Upload package** with the file, then **Upload**. The page is
shown again with the package in the list ([The setup wizard, 5.3.8](../../../install/05-setup-wizard.md#538-site-package)).

> **Tip**
> To make the installer use your copies instead of downloading, import the site package and every package it
> requires before you start. A required package is used as it is when its version is at least the required
> `min-version`. The kickstarter and `exp:install` use an imported site package as it is; the setup wizard shows only
> the remote entry when the index lists a higher version than the imported copy, and choosing it downloads the
> package afresh ([The setup wizard, 5.3.8](../../../install/05-setup-wizard.md#538-site-package)).
